author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 4th degree of consanguinity for marriage of two Spaniards. The man had seduced his third cousin.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 2nd and 3rd degrees of consanguinity for marriage of two Spaniards. The couple were first cousins on the mother's side: had been living together and had a child.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 3rd and 4th degrees of "affinity" for marriage of two Spaniards. The man's first wife was the second cousin of the father of the woman.

author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 3rd degree of consanguinity for marriage. The woman was the illegitimate daughter of the first cousin of the man's father.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 3rd and 4th degrees of consanguinity for marriage. The girl was second cousin of the man's mother.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 2nd degree of consanguinity for marriage. Publication of the banns had brought to light the unwelcome fact that the woman's mother was the illegitimate daughter of the man's grandfather.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 3rd and 4th degrees of consanguinity for marriage of a mestizo who had seduced his cousin.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 1st degree of "affinity" for marriage of two mestizos. The woman had been having illicit relations with a man, not knowing that he was the bastard brother of her future husband.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation for "copula ilicita" for marriage of a Spaniard to an Indian woman who had previously maintained illicit relations with the man's first cousin.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 2nd degree of "affinity" for marriage of two Indians. On the publication of the banns it transpired that the woman had previously held illicit relations with the first cousin of the man.

description: Dispensation of 2nd degree of "affinity" for marriage of two negroes. The man had committed adultery with a cousin of the woman.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 3rd degree of "affinity" for marriage of two Spaniards. The father of the first wife of the man was the great uncle of the woman.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 2nd degree of "affinity". Conceded after marriage of two Indians. The woman was the first cousin of the man's first wife.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of third degree of "affinity" for marriage of two Spaniards. The woman was the second cousin of the man's first wife.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 4th degree of "affinity" for "copula ilicita" permitting a couple to marry: the man's father being the second cousin of the woman's first husband.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 4th degree of "affinity" for marriage of two Indians. The man had previously maintained illicit relations with a first cousin of the woman, and had even committed adultery with the latter before his first wife died.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of "spiritual kindship" for marriage of two persons in Queretaao. The woman had unwittingly stood as godmother for an illegitimate child of the man at the christening.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Certified copy of dispensation for marriage of two Indians who were related through a previous marriage and the man had been having illicit relations with the cousin of the woman.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of second degree of consanguinity for marriage of two Indians, first cousins. They had already three children, and another Indian had once carried the woman off and kept possession of her for a week.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of publishing the banns for marriage of two Spaniards "to avoid scandal." The woman's first husband had been dead but a few months, and the man was the head clerk of her business.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation for publishing the banns for marriage of two Spaniards. The man was quite ill.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of second degree of consanguinity for marriage denied to two Indians. The man had seduced the woman who was his niece. He was sentenced to 25 clashes every Sunday for four Sundays at the door of the Parish Church; to six months imprisonment; to pay the mother of his unborn child $25.00 and to see her no more.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of the banns for the marriage of a Spaniard of noble blood with a poor free mulatto girl; to avoid scandal and trouble with his family. He had seduced her.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation for marriage of a mulatto and a mestiza who had been living together for nine years.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of the publication of banns before marriage. The relatives of the woman were opposed to the match, and the parties wished to be married secretly so that it would be too late for any active interference.

description: Dispensation of publication of banns of marriage for business reasons.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of publications of banns of marriage "to avoid scandal." The woman was a widow whose husband had not been dead a year.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of sin of adultery committed by two Indians of Tlaquietenange, permitting them to marry and legitimizing their children.
author: Barrientos, Manuel (Vicar General and acting Archbishop)

description: Dispensation of 3rd and 4th degrees of consanguinity for marriage of two Spaniards. They were third cousins on both sides of the house and the man was also the second cousin to the mother of the woman.
